rationale_bullets: Sayin's tape is the best in the graded set: 92.9 PFF on 438 dropbacks (B10 +1 -> 93.9 - a hair under the Texas-97 anchor's 95.0 adjusted), with an NCAA regular-season RECORD 78.4% completion rate, 3,610 yds, 32-8, a Heisman-finalist seat, and the Shaun Alexander award - as a redshirt freshman.

The named flaw is specific and showed up when it mattered (P6): off-script creation - 'unable to create when the pocket broke down' vs Indiana/Miami, with critical first-half INTs in both losses; 'the Craig Krenzel type plays' are the stated ask for 2026.
PS: 'held under wraps in some games... will probably top 4,000 yards this year and is a Heisman Frontrunner.' The new OC (Arthur Smith) tilts run-first and QB-friendly.
Depth: St. Clair (PS#3 recruit) + J.Martin (Maryland) - unproven but pedigree-deep.
91, H = between the p90 reference and the 97 anchor: elite proven volume with one documented ceiling question.
Bo Jackson returns off a 'surprise 1,000-yard freshman season' (P6): 86.6 PFF/178 att - between the p75/p90 RB references - 1,090 @ 6.1 with six 100-yard games; 'the most explosive back' (PS).

The room behind him is deep and young: West (76.5/59; 'borderline sensational' - Athlon), Ja'Kobi Jackson (67.0/27 at Florida; 509 @ 5.4 in 2024), rFr Rogers (PS#6), and Top100 ATH Bey (Day's Tyreek Hill/Curtis Samuel comps; slot/H hybrid).
GONE: short-yardage Donaldson (73.2/96, yr4) and Peoples (76.3/62, to Penn State) - rotation, not the engine.
Context: RBLK 93p line largely returns; run-game explosiveness (#73 - P6) is the named fix and the new OC's trademark is power run.
Weighted aggregate ~84 (~p77) = 76, M.

Jeremiah Smith returns for a final season: 90.7 PFF/362 routes (-> 89.7), unanimous All-American, 1,243/12 - 'many believe the best overall player in college football' (P6), on pace to break every school receiving record.

The subtraction is real: Tate (88.6/290) went FOURTH OVERALL (yr3 declare override), both All-B10 TEs left (Klare 69.3/302 - declare override; Kacmarek 77.5/115), and two 5* backups (Graham, Porter) portaled to Notre Dame - 'likely due to the breakout of five-star Chris Henry who surged all the way to the #2 role in spring' (P6).

The reload: Henry (5*, no volume - projection), Inniss (63.4/267) in the trio, McCuin (77.7/322 at UTSA, AAC +0 - All-AAC, 65/726), Parker (62.9/249 at LSU -> 68.9); TE via Welcing (61.0/203, all-league at NU), All-MAC M.Williams (74.4/164 -> 67.4), Top200 Roberts ('the spring hero').
Hartline's conveyor-belt prior: 'at least two future first-round picks in the room' every year since 2019 (P6).
Mechanical aggregate ~76.6 sits just under the room's own 2025 p97 print. 86, M = top-5 room: one transcendent player + projection at #2/TE.

rationale_bullets: Four returning starters, ALL FOUR All-B10, 89-91 combined career starts - 'one of the most veteran lines in America' (P6); 'a clear Joe Moore Award contender in 2026' (PS).

Siereveld (83.5 PFF/810 -> 82.5) did not allow a single sack all season - 'their best shot at an All-America season' (P6); Hinzman (73.6/841; yr4 override RETURNS, double-print), Montgomery (73.4/837), Daniels (66.1/761).
The departure is addition-by-subtraction: Tshabola (56.3/607 - the room's worst full-volume tape) to Kentucky; the 5th spot is a Top200 battle (Padilla 73.7/128 vs Moore 69.7/150 vs VanSickle).
The honest counterweight: Indiana + Miami got 10 sacks and held OSU to 2.1 ypc - PBLK 64p as-played is the one soft number in the profile (RBLK 93p).
Weighted aggregate ~73.3 (~p78) + pedigree mass + settled two-deep = 80, H.

rationale_bullets: The two best tapes left: Curry (90.6/610; 11 sk, 16.5 TFL) and 1st-team AA McDonald (86.2/448; rd-2 - a yr3 declare the override catches), plus Malone, Atkinson, and EIGHT portal backups (PS).

What returns is credible: Jackson Jr. (72.7/549 -> 82.7 - 'the only returning starter,' himself a yr4 override RETURNS documented by both books), W.Smith Jr. (72.6/224 -> 82.6), Grady (74.8/104), and 5* Houston (59.6/324 -> 69.6; 'ready for a breakout season at tackle' - P6).
The imports are the reload: both Alabama linemen - J.Smith (55.3/422, SEC +8 -> 63.3; pedigree over tape) and Russaw (67.6/215 -> 75.6) - plus Top100 UCF starter Walker (70.7/495, B12 +3 -> 73.7).
Post-adjustment the room carries FIVE pieces at 73+ - Kentucky-91-anchor breadth without the 90+ star; Larry Johnson's development record is the qualitative floor (Athlon).
76, M - even with 'zero returning starters' framing, the adjusted quality and pipeline hold a top-30 grade; PS: 'loaded with 4th and 5th year players and, of course, talent.'

rationale_bullets: The teardown is total: ALL THREE starters gone - two All-American FIRST-ROUNDERS (S.Styles 88.6/663; Reese 76.5/651 - yr3 declare override) plus the NB. P6: 'even the greatest reloading programs would struggle here.'

The reload is the best available anywhere: Pierce (82.2/263 -> 98.2 adjusted - elite rotational tape at a moderate sample; PS#14), Alliegro (62.3/449 at Wisconsin -> 78.3; 'the #3 linebacker transfer'), Top100s Pettijohn (66.6/77) and Alford ('the early standout' in spring), and the #1 LB recruit in the class (5* Cincere Johnson).
PS's read is the grade's shape: 'they remain solid, but are less experienced and a concern.'
LB caution (noisiest unit) + moderate samples + the +16 offset doing real work = 64, M - clearly above average on pedigree and Pierce's tape, two tiers below what left.

rationale_bullets: The losses are historic: Downs (87.5/682 - a top-7 pick, yr3 declare override; 'one of their best safeties of all-time' - P6) + 1st-tm B10 CB Igbinosun (82.0/655; rd-2) + the NB, plus a five-man portal wave (Delane/Scott/West/Hartford/Haddad).

What returns is real: McClain (78.1/708 -> 84.1; 'star potential'), Mathews (62.2/695 -> 68.2; 'welcoming his new role as the top corner' - Athlon), and 5* SOPH Sanchez (60.8/323; 'poised to be yet another Buckeye great'; PS: 'could be that next #1 DC').

The imports address safety directly: two 2nd-team All-ACC pieces - Little (69.1/674 at FSU -> 70.1) and T.Moore (Duke; limited 2025 volume - prior-year honors carry the case) - plus 5* Timmons and Top100 Bradford.
Context: PDR #15, COV 91p in 2025; PS: 'may drop some.' Walton's development record and the DBU pipeline are the qualitative floor.
Mechanical aggregate ~72.9 (~p75) = 72, M - exactly the WSU-72 anchor's position, matching Indiana's room.
